diagnosis: The scenario failed the Weak Arm gate because all rollouts correctly defaulted to the baseline/draft values (e.g., 'backend engineer', 4 shifts, 'Eastern' time, and no security observer) without any agent interaction. This indicates that the decision-maker can successfully complete the task using only the shared public facts (S1, S2, S3) by following the default settings, making the hidden information provided by agents A2, A3, A4, and A5 unnecessary for a successful outcome.

fix_instructions: To make the scenario require multi-agent coordination, the baseline/publicly available information must be intentionally ambiguous or incorrect so that the model cannot reach the correct settlement without the private facts. Specifically: 1. Ensure the public draft does not specify a primary engineer, forcing the model to rely on PF1 to select Mina. 2. Set the public fatigue policy to an undefined or highly variable value so PF2 is required to pin it to 2 shifts. 3. Make the public customer agreement use a generic timezone or omit the window entirely so PF3 is required to set it to Pacific. 4. Remove the 'no security observer' default in the public context so PF4 is required to assign Ravi.
